title: Embeddings and Vector Search Handbook
summary: Quick revision notes on what embeddings are, how similarity metrics and normalisation work, how to pick an embedding model, how HNSW and IVF indexes trade recall for speed, and how metadata filtering interacts with ANN search.

chapters.title: What an Embedding Is
points: Embedding: a fixed-length float vector produced by a model so that semantically similar inputs land close together in space
Mental model: meaning becomes geometry; distance or angle between vectors is the similarity signal, not any single dimension
Vectors are only comparable when made by the same model and version; mixing models gives meaningless scores
Same pipeline embeds documents at index time and queries at search time (query-side prefixes like 'query:' vs 'passage:' if the model requires)
Core workflow: chunk text, embed each chunk, store vector plus metadata, embed query, return top-k nearest

chapters.title: Distance Metrics and Normalisation
points: Cosine similarity = dot(a,b)/(|a||b|); measures angle only, range -1 to 1, ignores magnitude
Dot product = sum(a_i*b_i); rewards both angle and magnitude, so longer vectors score higher
Euclidean (L2) = sqrt(sum((a_i-b_i)^2)); straight-line distance, lower is closer, sensitive to magnitude
L2-normalise vectors to unit length (v / |v|): then cosine == dot product, and L2^2 = 2 - 2*cos, so all three give the same ranking
Match the metric to how the model was trained (check the model card); most text embedding models are trained for cosine, so normalise and use dot for speed

chapters.title: Choosing an Embedding Model and Dimensions
points: Selection criteria: retrieval quality on your own domain data (not just MTEB rank), max input tokens, language coverage, latency, cost, licence
Dimensions: higher (1536, 3072) gives more capacity but costs memory = N * dims * 4 bytes for float32 and slower search
Matryoshka models let you truncate vectors (e.g. 3072 to 256) with small quality loss; re-normalise after truncating
Quantisation shrinks storage: float16 halves it, int8 cuts 4x, binary cuts 32x, usually with a rescoring pass on full vectors
Changing the model or dimension means re-embedding the whole corpus; version your index and plan a dual-write migration

chapters.title: Vector Indexes: Flat, HNSW and IVF
points: Flat (brute force): compares the query to every vector; exact, 100% recall, fine up to roughly 100k vectors, O(N) per query
HNSW: layered proximity graph; search enters at the sparse top layer and greedily descends to the dense bottom layer; fast, high recall, high memory
HNSW knobs: M (links per node; more means better recall and more RAM), efConstruction (build quality), efSearch (candidates explored at query time; raise for recall, costs latency)
IVF: k-means clusters vectors into nlist cells; a query probes only the nprobe nearest centroids; needs a training step and uses less memory than HNSW
IVF-PQ compresses vectors with product quantisation for huge corpora at some recall loss; nprobe=1 is fast but misses neighbours near cell borders

chapters.title: ANN Recall Trade-offs and Metadata Filtering
points: ANN trades exactness for speed; recall@k = fraction of true top-k (from flat search) that the index returns
Measure recall by running exact search on a sample of queries and comparing; tune efSearch or nprobe until recall hits target (e.g. 95%) at acceptable p95 latency
Post-filtering: search top-k then drop non-matching results; can return fewer than k, or zero, when the filter is selective

Pre-filtering or filtered-HNSW: apply the filter during traversal; correct counts, but very selective filters can slow search or fragment the graph, so fall back to brute force on the small filtered set
Common mistakes: no recall measurement, filtering after a small top-k, mixing metrics between index and query, forgetting to normalise, re-embedding with a different model without rebuilding

chapters.title: Embeddings and Vector Search Cheat Sheet
points: Similarity: cosine = angle; dot = angle times magnitude; L2 = distance; normalised vectors make all three rank identically
Memory: N * dims * 4 bytes (float32); 1M x 1536 is about 6 GB before index overhead
Index choice: flat under ~100k; HNSW for low latency and high recall with enough RAM; IVF(-PQ) for huge or memory-bound corpora
Tuning dials: HNSW efSearch up = recall up, latency up; IVF nprobe up = recall up, latency up; always report recall@k and p95
Checklist: same model for docs and queries, normalise if cosine, set the index metric to match, overfetch or pre-filter when filtering, re-embed everything on model change
